# Voice Agent Linter rules

> Informational, not legal advice. Laws change and courts interpret them; confirm with a lawyer licensed in the jurisdiction before relying on any rule here.

Data: [`data/voice-linter/rules.json`](../data/voice-linter/rules.json). 37 rules. Each one catches a failure seen on real calls. Vendor rules cite the vendor's documentation, legal rules cite the law, as of 2026-10-11.

| Id | Severity | Category | Platforms | Reads | Rule | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `no-live-date` | high | dates | all | prompt and config | The agent is never told today’s date | Inject the live date and time with the timezone into the prompt using the platform’s variable, and tell the agent to trust it over its own sense of the date. |
| `date-without-year` | medium | dates | all | prompt | A date is written without its year | Write every one-time date with its year. For a date that repeats every year, say so ("every December 25"). Have tools return dates with the year and tell the agent to pass them through exactly as written. |
| `date-param-no-format` | medium | dates | all | config | A tool takes a date with no format | Describe the exact format (YYYY-MM-DD, or ISO 8601 with offset) and say the value must be copied from what the availability tool returned, never constructed. |
| `phone-as-numerals` | medium | speech | all | prompt | A phone number is written as numerals | Write phone numbers in the prompt as words, comma separated, with a period between groups, and tell the agent to say any identifier the same way. A text replacement rule in the voice settings, where the platform has one, catches what the model still emits. |
| `email-written-raw` | medium | speech | all | prompt | An email address is written the way it is typed | Write the spoken form: words for the parts, "at", "dot", and the word "dash" for a hyphen. Spell it with anchors only when the words will not do. |

| `no-spelling-protocol` | high | spelling | all | prompt and config | The agent collects names or emails with no spelling protocol | Add a spelling protocol: words first for emails, anchored letters when spelling, ask callers to spell the same way, read back once from exactly what you will type, never add a joined-up version, and after two failed readbacks switch to a phone number. |
| `bare-letter-spelling` | medium | spelling | all | prompt | Spelling uses bare letters or letter sounds | Replace bare-letter spelling with anchored spelling, using ordinary anchor words. |
| `english-anchors-multilingual` | low | spelling | all | prompt | English spelling anchors in a multilingual agent | Tell the agent to use anchor words in the language of the call and to drop English-only respellings outside English. |

## Rule detail

### `no-live-date`: The agent is never told today’s date

**Severity:** high. **Category:** dates.

A language model has no clock. Asked to book "Thursday", it fills in a year from its training data, often one or two years in the past, and a booking tool that checks against the real calendar refuses every date it is offered. The transcript reads like a broken integration or a lead-time rule, so the real cause is easy to miss, and it does not show up in testing done the same week the prompt was written.

- Bad: `You book appointments for Acme Plumbing. Offer the caller the next open day.`

- Good: `Right now it is {{"now" | date: "%A, %B %d, %Y, %I:%M %p", "America/Denver"}}. Trust this over any sense you have of the date.`

**Fix:** Inject the live date and time with the timezone into the prompt using the platform’s variable, and tell the agent to trust it over its own sense of the date.

**Sources:** [Vapi docs: dynamic variables ({{now}}, {{date}}, {{year}} and the LiquidJS date filter with a timezone)](https://docs.vapi.ai/assistants/dynamic-variables) (as of 2026-10-11); [Retell docs: dynamic variables ({{current_time}}, {{current_time_timezone}}, {{current_calendar}})](https://docs.retellai.com/build/dynamic-variables) (as of 2026-10-11); [ElevenLabs Agents docs: system dynamic variables ({{system__time}}, {{system__time_utc}}, {{system__timezone}})](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/agents-platform/customization/personalization/dynamic-variables) (as of 2026-10-11)

### `date-without-year`: A date is written without its year

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** dates.

A date with no year ("closed March 3", "Wed, Aug 20") is completed by the model, which guesses the year. When the guess lands in the past, every downstream check (calendar, booking, holiday rule) fails for a reason the agent cannot see. The same applies to dates a tool returns: if they carry no year, the model invents one before sending them back.

- Bad: `We are closed March 3 for inventory.`

- Good: `We are closed on Tuesday, March 3, 2027 for inventory.`

**Fix:** Write every one-time date with its year. For a date that repeats every year, say so ("every December 25"). Have tools return dates with the year and tell the agent to pass them through exactly as written.

### `date-param-no-format`: A tool takes a date with no format

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** dates.

A tool parameter called date, day or time with no stated format lets the model construct the value itself, which is where the wrong year and the wrong timezone come from. A stated format plus an instruction to copy dates from the availability tool closes it.

- Bad: `"date": { "type": "string" }`

- Good: `"date": { "type": "string", "description": "The day exactly as check_availability returned it, YYYY-MM-DD, including the year." }`

**Fix:** Describe the exact format (YYYY-MM-DD, or ISO 8601 with offset) and say the value must be copied from what the availability tool returned, never constructed.

### `phone-as-numerals`: A phone number is written as numerals

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** speech.

Whatever the prompt writes, the model tends to repeat, and text to speech reads numerals as quantities: 2023 becomes a year, 200 becomes "two hundred", a lone 0 can come out as a sound that is not a word. A caller writing down a number cannot tell which digit was garbled.

- Bad: `Our office line is (212) 555-0134.`

- Good: `Our office line is two, one, two. five, five, five. zero, one, three, four.`

**Fix:** Write phone numbers in the prompt as words, comma separated, with a period between groups, and tell the agent to say any identifier the same way. A text replacement rule in the voice settings, where the platform has one, catches what the model still emits.

### `email-written-raw`: An email address is written the way it is typed

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** speech.

An address like info@acme-co.com is read aloud with symbols and run-together words that callers mishear. Hyphens are often read as "minus". The spoken form has to be written out so the agent says it the same way every time.

- Bad: `Send documents to info@acme-co.com.`

- Good: `Send documents to info at acme dash co dot com.`

**Fix:** Write the spoken form: words for the parts, "at", "dot", and the word "dash" for a hyphen. Spell it with anchors only when the words will not do.

### `url-written-raw`: A web address is written with its scheme

**Severity:** low. **Category:** speech.

Text to speech reads "https://www." letter by letter or as "h t t p s colon slash slash", which nobody can act on over the phone.

- Bad: `Book online at https://www.acme.com/book.`

- Good: `Book online at acme dot com, slash book.`

**Fix:** Write the address as it should be spoken, without the scheme or "www".

### `hyphen-range`: A range is written with a hyphen

**Severity:** low. **Category:** speech.

Ranges like "9-5" or "Mon-Fri" are read as "nine minus five" or skipped, depending on the voice. Hours are the most common thing a caller asks for.

- Bad: `Hours: Mon-Fri 8am-5pm.`

- Good: `Hours: Monday through Friday, eight in the morning to five in the evening.`

**Fix:** Write ranges in words: "Monday through Friday", "eight to five".

### `long-digit-string`: A long number is written as digits

**Severity:** low. **Category:** speech.

A zip code, account number or code written as digits is read as a quantity ("fifty-nine thousand nine hundred one"). Identifiers have to be read digit by digit to be written down.

- Bad: `We serve zip code 59901.`

- Good: `We serve zip code five, nine, nine, zero, one.`

**Fix:** Write identifiers as words, digit by digit. Prices and quantities can stay as figures.

### `markdown-output`: The prompt asks for formatted output

**Severity:** low. **Category:** speech.

Bullet points, bold, headings, tables and emojis make no sense spoken and some voices read the symbols aloud. Lists read aloud also lose callers.

- Bad: `Answer with a bulleted list of our services.`

- Good: `Name the two services that fit what they asked for, in one sentence.`

**Fix:** Ask for short spoken sentences and at most two options at a time.

### `no-spelling-protocol`: The agent collects names or emails with no spelling protocol

**Severity:** high. **Category:** spelling.

Speech recognition turns a name or an email said at speed into the nearest ordinary word, so the agent writes down something that sounds right and is wrong. Measured on recordings run back through speech recognition: anchored letters ("b as in boy") came back letter perfect at studio and phone quality, bare letters mostly survived, and letter sounds ("bee", "ay") came back wrong. An agent with no protocol also tends to read the value back several ways, and the caller hears only the broken one.

- Bad: `Collect the caller’s email address.`

- Good: `Say email addresses as words first ("john. smith. at gmail dot com"). If you must spell, use anchors: "b as in boy. i as in igloo." Read it back once, ask if it is right, then stop. If it is wrong twice, take a phone number instead.`

**Fix:** Add a spelling protocol: words first for emails, anchored letters when spelling, ask callers to spell the same way, read back once from exactly what you will type, never add a joined-up version, and after two failed readbacks switch to a phone number.

### `bare-letter-spelling`: Spelling uses bare letters or letter sounds

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** spelling.

Spelling "one character at a time" or with letter sounds ("bee, eye, zee") is the version that failed in measurement: "ay" is heard as I, and the corruption sounds careful, so nobody catches it.

- Bad: `Spell the email back one character at a time.`

- Good: `Spell it back with anchors: "j as in john. o as in ocean."`

**Fix:** Replace bare-letter spelling with anchored spelling, using ordinary anchor words.

### `english-anchors-multilingual`: English spelling anchors in a multilingual agent

**Severity:** low. **Category:** spelling.

An agent that answers in the caller’s language but spells with English anchors ("b as in boy") gives a Spanish speaker nothing to hold on to. The anchors have to travel with the language, as does any pronunciation respelling.

- Bad: `Reply in the caller’s language. Spell with anchors: b as in boy.`

- Good: `Spell with anchors in the language of the call: in Spanish, "b de Barcelona".`

**Fix:** Tell the agent to use anchor words in the language of the call and to drop English-only respellings outside English.

### `claims-to-be-human`: The prompt tells the agent to pass as human

**Severity:** critical. **Category:** disclosure.

An AI agent that says it is a person, or is told never to admit it is AI, deceives the caller. The FCC treats AI-generated voices as artificial voices under the TCPA, Utah requires disclosure when a consumer asks, and California requires bots used to sell to disclose that they are bots.

- Bad: `You are Sam, a real person on the front desk. Never reveal that you are an AI.`

- Good: `You are Sam, the AI assistant for Acme. If anyone asks whether you are a person, say plainly that you are an AI.`

**Fix:** Remove the instruction. State that the agent is an AI and must say so plainly when asked.

**Sources:** [FCC Declaratory Ruling FCC 24-17 (Feb. 8, 2024): AI-generated voices are "artificial" voices under the TCPA](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-24-17A1.pdf) (as of 2026-10-11); [Utah Code 13-75-103 and 13-75-104 (S.B. 226, 2025, effective May 7, 2025): disclose generative AI when a consumer asks; safe harbor for disclosure at the outset](https://le.utah.gov/Session/2025/bills/enrolled/SB0226.pdf) (as of 2026-10-11); [California Business and Professions Code 17941: bots used to sell goods or services must disclose that they are bots](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=17941) (as of 2026-10-11)

### `no-ai-disclosure`: No AI disclosure

**Severity:** high. **Category:** disclosure.

Neither the prompt nor the opening line says the caller is talking to an AI. Disclosure at the start of the call is the safe harbor under Utah’s law, the FCC treats AI voices as artificial voices for outbound calls, and callers who find out later trust the business less. When the agent only discloses on request, outbound calls to strangers are where it matters most.

- Bad: `Thanks for calling Acme, this is Sam. How can I help?`

- Good: `Thanks for calling Acme. I’m Sam, Acme’s AI assistant. How can I help?`

**Fix:** Say it in the first or second sentence of the opener, and tell the agent to confirm it plainly whenever asked. Check every language variant of the opener, since translations tend to drop it.

**Sources:** [Utah Code 13-75-103 and 13-75-104 (S.B. 226, 2025, effective May 7, 2025): disclose generative AI when a consumer asks; safe harbor for disclosure at the outset](https://le.utah.gov/Session/2025/bills/enrolled/SB0226.pdf) (as of 2026-10-11); [FCC Declaratory Ruling FCC 24-17 (Feb. 8, 2024): AI-generated voices are "artificial" voices under the TCPA](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-24-17A1.pdf) (as of 2026-10-11); [47 CFR 64.1200(b): artificial or prerecorded voice calls must identify the business at the start and give a phone number](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-47/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-64/subpart-L/section-64.1200) (as of 2026-10-11)

### `no-recording-notice`: No recording notice

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** disclosure.

Voice platforms record and transcribe calls, often by default. Federal law and most states allow recording with one party’s consent, but California and several other states require every party to consent to recording a confidential call, and callers can be in any state. A short notice in the opener covers it.

- Bad: `Thanks for calling Acme, I’m Sam, Acme’s AI assistant.`

- Good: `Thanks for calling Acme, I’m Sam, Acme’s AI assistant. This call is recorded.`

**Fix:** Add a recording notice to the opener, or turn recording off if you do not use it.

**Sources:** [California Penal Code 632: recording a confidential communication requires the consent of all parties](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PEN&sectionNum=632) (as of 2026-10-11); [18 U.S.C. 2511(2)(d): federal one-party consent to record](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/2511) (as of 2026-10-11); [Vapi API reference: create assistant (firstMessage, firstMessageMode, maxDurationSeconds default 600, endCallPhrases, artifactPlan.recordingEnabled default true)](https://docs.vapi.ai/api-reference/assistants/create) (as of 2026-10-11)

### `scripted-tool-start`: A tool has a scripted start line

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** turn_taking.

When the model speaks its own lead-in and calls a tool in the same turn, and the tool also has a scripted "request start" line, the two collide. Observed on live calls: the tool returned in under a second, no model request followed, and the caller sat in silence until they hung up. Empty start lines with a model-spoken beat, or a scripted line with no model lead-in, both worked; the combination did not.

- Bad: `"messages": [{ "type": "request-start", "content": "One moment while I check the calendar." }]`

- Good: `"messages": [{ "type": "request-start", "content": "" }] with the prompt saying what the agent is doing, never a result, before the tool returns.`

**Fix:** Set request-start content to empty and let the model say a short beat about what it is doing. Never let it state a result ("Friday works") before the tool answers.

**Sources:** [Vapi docs: custom tools (function name, description and JSON Schema parameters; request start, complete, failed and delayed messages; results returned as strings)](https://docs.vapi.ai/tools/custom-tools) (as of 2026-10-11)

### `stall-phrases`: The prompt scripts stall phrases

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** turn_taking.

Scripted stalls ("hold on a sec", "let me check on that", "bear with me") fill a gap the caller would not have noticed, sound like a dropped call on a phone line, and on some platforms collide with tool messages to wedge the turn.

- Bad: `Before checking availability, say "Hold on one moment while I look that up."`

- Good: `Check availability, then give the two soonest times. Say what you are doing in a few words only if the lookup takes noticeably long.`

**Fix:** Remove scripted stalls. Let the answer be the next thing the caller hears.

### `silent-opener`: The agent waits in silence when the call connects

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** turn_taking.

With no first message, the agent waits for the caller to speak first. On an inbound business line the caller expects a greeting, so both sides wait and many callers hang up. Vapi documents that an unspecified firstMessage makes the assistant wait for the user; an empty Retell begin_message or ElevenLabs first_message does the same.

- Bad: `"firstMessage": ""`

- Good: `"firstMessage": "Thanks for calling Acme, I’m Sam, Acme’s AI assistant. How can I help?"`

**Fix:** Set a short first message for inbound agents. Leave it empty only on outbound calls where the person answering should speak first.

**Sources:** [Vapi API reference: create assistant (firstMessage, firstMessageMode, maxDurationSeconds default 600, endCallPhrases, artifactPlan.recordingEnabled default true)](https://docs.vapi.ai/api-reference/assistants/create) (as of 2026-10-11); [Retell API reference: create Retell LLM (general_prompt, begin_message, general_tools)](https://docs.retellai.com/api-references/create-retell-llm) (as of 2026-10-11); [ElevenLabs API reference: create agent (conversation_config.agent.first_message, prompt, tools; tts.model_id)](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/agents-platform/api-reference/agents/create) (as of 2026-10-11)

### `long-opener`: The opener is long

**Severity:** low. **Category:** turn_taking.

Callers start talking over a long greeting, interruptions cut it off, and the disclosure or the question at its end gets lost.

- Bad: `Thank you so much for calling Acme Plumbing and Heating, proudly serving the valley since 1982, where our licensed technicians...`

- Good: `Thanks for calling Acme. I’m Sam, Acme’s AI assistant. How can I help?`

**Fix:** Keep the opener under about 25 words: who, AI disclosure, recording notice if needed, one question.

### `tool-no-description`: A tool has no description

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** tools.

The model decides when to call a tool, and what to put in it, from its description. Without one it calls the tool at the wrong time or not at all.

- Bad: `{ "name": "book" }`

- Good: `{ "name": "book_appointment", "description": "Books a confirmed slot. Call only after the caller agrees to a time from check_availability. Returns booked: true and the confirmation text to read back." }`

**Fix:** Say when to call it, what each input must be, and what it returns.

### `tool-param-untyped`: A tool parameter has no type

**Severity:** high. **Category:** tools.

An untyped parameter can arrive as anything, and some platforms drop the whole argument object when the schema is not one they handle.

- Bad: `"phone": { "description": "Caller phone" }`

- Good: `"phone": { "type": "string", "description": "Ten digits, no punctuation." }`

**Fix:** Give every parameter a JSON Schema type.

### `tool-param-undescribed`: A tool parameter has no description

**Severity:** low. **Category:** tools.

The parameter name is the only guide the model has, so formats and allowed values get guessed.

- Bad: `"service": { "type": "string" }`

- Good: `"service": { "type": "string", "description": "One of: drain cleaning, water heater, leak repair. Exactly as written." }`

**Fix:** Describe each parameter: format, allowed values, where the value comes from.

### `tool-required-missing`: A required parameter is not defined

**Severity:** high. **Category:** tools.

The schema requires a field that has no definition under properties, so a valid call can never be made, or the platform rejects the schema.

- Bad: `"required": ["email"], "properties": { "name": {...} }`

- Good: `"required": ["email"], "properties": { "email": {...}, "name": {...} }`

**Fix:** Define every required field under properties, or remove it from required.

### `tool-result-unstated`: A tool does not say what it returns

**Severity:** low. **Category:** tools.

When neither the tool description nor the prompt names the fields a tool returns, the model guesses at the result, and a refusal or partial result is read as success. Tools that return explicit named fields (booked: true or false, a reason, the open times) let the agent answer from facts.

- Bad: `"description": "Checks the calendar."`

- Good: `"description": "Checks the calendar. Returns open_days: a list of full dates with the year, each with times; pass a date back exactly as written."`

**Fix:** Return explicit named fields and say in the description what they are. Include the reason and the real alternatives on every refusal.

### `vapi-nested-item-enum`: An enum inside array items (Vapi)

**Severity:** high. **Category:** tools.

A Vapi function parameter of type array whose items carry an enum was observed to arrive at the webhook as an empty object: not just that field, every field, including required ones. The config saved, read back and listed cleanly; the only trace was empty arguments in the call history. A plain top-level string enum works. This is an observed platform behavior, not one the docs describe.

- Bad: `"services": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string", "enum": ["drain", "heater"] } }`

- Good: `"services": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" }, "description": "Any of: drain, heater. Exactly as written." }`

**Fix:** Remove the enum from items, list the legal values in the parameter description, and validate on your server.

**Sources:** [Vapi docs: custom tools (function name, description and JSON Schema parameters; request start, complete, failed and delayed messages; results returned as strings)](https://docs.vapi.ai/tools/custom-tools) (as of 2026-10-11)

### `vapi-flat-analysis-keys`: Flat analysisPlan prompt keys (Vapi)

**Severity:** high. **Category:** analysis.

analysisPlan.summaryPrompt, structuredDataPrompt and structuredDataSchema are accepted and stored, but an assistant created with them came back with summaryPlan and successEvaluationPlan disabled, so call.analysis.summary was empty on every real call. A synthetic webhook test passes because the test supplies its own summary.

- Bad: `"analysisPlan": { "summaryPrompt": "Summarize the call." }`

- Good: `"analysisPlan": { "summaryPlan": { "enabled": true, "messages": [{ "role": "system", "content": "Summarize this call: {{transcript}}" }] } }`

**Fix:** Use the plan objects with enabled: true and messages, then read the assistant back and confirm the plan is enabled. For new setups Vapi recommends structured outputs.

**Sources:** [Vapi docs: call analysis (summaryPlan, structuredDataPlan, successEvaluationPlan stored in call.analysis; structured outputs recommended for new setups)](https://docs.vapi.ai/assistants/call-analysis) (as of 2026-10-11); [Vapi docs: structured outputs](https://docs.vapi.ai/assistants/structured-outputs) (as of 2026-10-11)

### `vapi-analysis-plan-off`: An analysis plan is defined but disabled (Vapi)

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** analysis.

A plan with messages and enabled: false never runs, so the dashboard shows the prompt and the call shows nothing.

- Bad: `"summaryPlan": { "enabled": false, "messages": [...] }`

- Good: `"summaryPlan": { "enabled": true, "messages": [...] }`

**Fix:** Set enabled to true, or delete the plan.

**Sources:** [Vapi docs: call analysis (summaryPlan, structuredDataPlan, successEvaluationPlan stored in call.analysis; structured outputs recommended for new setups)](https://docs.vapi.ai/assistants/call-analysis) (as of 2026-10-11)

### `vapi-analysis-no-transcript`: An analysis plan never sees the transcript (Vapi)

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** analysis.

Plan messages are templates. Without {{transcript}} in them, the analysis model receives the instruction and none of the call, and answers anyway.

- Bad: `{ "role": "system", "content": "Summarize the call." }`

- Good: `{ "role": "system", "content": "Summarize the call.\n\n{{transcript}}" }`

**Fix:** Interpolate {{transcript}} in the plan’s messages.

**Sources:** [Vapi docs: call analysis (summaryPlan, structuredDataPlan, successEvaluationPlan stored in call.analysis; structured outputs recommended for new setups)](https://docs.vapi.ai/assistants/call-analysis) (as of 2026-10-11)

### `turbo-tts-stutter`: ElevenLabs Turbo voice model

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** voice.

On one production voice, eleven_turbo_v2_5 inserted words that were not in the text in about 8 of 96 takes, including a duplicated digit inside an email readback, which defeats any spelling protocol. Changing stability or speed did not move the rate. eleven_multilingual_v2 came back clean on 84 takes; streaming latency optimization at level 2 kept the extra delay to about 130 milliseconds. Measured on one voice: test yours.

- Bad: `"voice": { "provider": "11labs", "model": "eleven_turbo_v2_5" }`

- Good: `"voice": { "provider": "11labs", "model": "eleven_multilingual_v2", "optimizeStreamingLatency": 2 }`

**Fix:** Synthesize your readback lines at least 24 times with your exact voice settings, transcribe them, and flag any take with extra words. If Turbo inserts words, move to a model that does not and use the platform’s latency setting to recover speed.

**Sources:** [ElevenLabs docs: models (Turbo, Flash and Multilingual families)](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/models) (as of 2026-10-11)

### `no-human-fallback`: No way to reach a person

**Severity:** high. **Category:** call_control.

Every agent meets a caller it cannot help: an emergency, an angry customer, a question outside its knowledge. With no transfer and no message-taking path, it either loops or invents an answer.

- Bad: `Answer questions about our services.`

- Good: `If you cannot help, or the caller asks for a person, take their name and number and say someone will call back today, or transfer to the office line.`

**Fix:** Add a transfer tool or forwarding number, or at minimum a message-taking path with a stated callback time, and tell the agent when to use it.

**Sources:** [Vapi docs: default tools (transferCall, endCall)](https://docs.vapi.ai/tools/default-tools) (as of 2026-10-11); [Retell docs: transfer call function](https://docs.retellai.com/build/single-multi-prompt/transfer-call) (as of 2026-10-11); [ElevenLabs Agents docs: transfer to human system tool](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/agents-platform/customization/tools/system-tools/transfer-to-human) (as of 2026-10-11)

### `no-end-call`: The agent cannot end the call

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** call_control.

Without an end-call tool or phrase, the agent fills silence after the caller is done, or the call runs until the platform’s timeout, which costs minutes and sounds broken.

- Bad: `No end-call tool, no instruction to finish.`

- Good: `An endCall tool, and "When the caller has what they need, say goodbye and end the call."`

**Fix:** Enable the platform’s end-call tool and say when to use it.

**Sources:** [Vapi docs: default tools (transferCall, endCall)](https://docs.vapi.ai/tools/default-tools) (as of 2026-10-11); [Retell docs: end call function](https://docs.retellai.com/build/single-multi-prompt/end-call) (as of 2026-10-11); [ElevenLabs Agents docs: end call system tool](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/agents-platform/customization/tools/system-tools/end-call) (as of 2026-10-11)

### `vapi-max-duration-default`: Calls are cut at ten minutes (Vapi default)

**Severity:** low. **Category:** call_control.

maxDurationSeconds defaults to 600. A long intake or a caller on hold is cut mid-sentence at ten minutes.

- Bad: `No maxDurationSeconds.`

- Good: `"maxDurationSeconds": 1800`

**Fix:** Set maxDurationSeconds to the longest call you expect, with headroom.

**Sources:** [Vapi API reference: create assistant (firstMessage, firstMessageMode, maxDurationSeconds default 600, endCallPhrases, artifactPlan.recordingEnabled default true)](https://docs.vapi.ai/api-reference/assistants/create) (as of 2026-10-11)

### `vapi-free-number-outbound`: Outbound calling from a free Vapi number

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** call_control.

The prompt reads as an outbound caller and the config uses a Vapi-provided number. Vapi documents that free Vapi numbers are inbound only, and outbound calls through Vapi-provided numbers have been refused after a small daily count. Calls fail before the agent ever speaks.

- Bad: `"phoneNumber": { "provider": "vapi" } with "You are calling customers to confirm..."`

- Good: `An imported Twilio, Telnyx or Vonage number for outbound.`

**Fix:** Import a number from a carrier for outbound calls.

**Sources:** [Vapi docs: free telephony ("Free Vapi numbers are inbound only")](https://docs.vapi.ai/free-telephony) (as of 2026-10-11)

### `unfilled-placeholder`: An unfilled placeholder

**Severity:** high. **Category:** hygiene.

Template leftovers like [Business Name], {company}, XXX or TBD are read aloud to callers. Platforms fill double-brace variables only; single braces and brackets are spoken literally.

- Bad: `Welcome to [Business Name]! We are open {hours}.`

- Good: `Welcome to Acme! We are open Monday through Friday, eight to five.`

**Fix:** Fill the value, or use the platform’s double-brace variable and pass it on every call.

### `secret-in-prompt`: A secret is in the prompt

**Severity:** critical. **Category:** hygiene.

Anything in the prompt or a tool description can be repeated to a caller who asks the right way. API keys, bearer tokens and passwords belong in server-side config.

- Bad: `Use API key sk-live-abc123... to look up orders.`

- Good: `Call lookup_order; the server holds the key.`

**Fix:** Remove it, rotate the key now, and move it to a server-side secret.

### `prompt-length`: The prompt is very long

**Severity:** low. **Category:** hygiene.

Every turn of a voice call sends the whole prompt. Very long prompts add latency to every reply and bury rules in the middle, where models weight them least.

- Bad: `A 60,000 character prompt with the full FAQ pasted in.`

- Good: `A focused prompt, with the FAQ in a knowledge base or a lookup tool.`

**Fix:** Move reference material to a knowledge base or a tool, and put the rules that must never break at the end.

### `contradictory-instructions`: Two instructions contradict each other

**Severity:** medium. **Category:** hygiene.

When one line says always and another says never about the same thing, the model picks one per call, so behavior changes from call to call.

- Bad: `Always quote a price. ... Never give prices over the phone.`

- Good: `Never give prices over the phone; offer to have the owner call back with a quote.`

**Fix:** Keep one instruction and delete the other, or state the exception explicitly.
